questions.question: What is a geometric proof?
choices: A list of measurements from one example
A logical argument based on accepted facts and justified steps

questions.question: What is a conjecture?
choices: A proven theorem in every case
A statement proposed from patterns that still needs justification

questions.question: What is a counterexample?
choices: One case that agrees with the claim
One valid case that disproves a universal claim
A theorem that uses the same words

questions.question: Which property supports 'if a = b and b = c, then a = c'?
What is given information in a proof?
choices: Every feature that appears visually true
Any unmeasured length in the picture
Facts stated or marked as assumptions for the problem

questions.question: Which fact justifies that a segment equals itself in length?
What distinguishes a theorem from a conjecture?
choices: A theorem has a proof under its stated assumptions

questions.question: Why is measuring one drawn triangle insufficient to prove a claim about all triangles?
choices: One example does not establish every possible case
A drawing cannot show a triangle

questions.question: What is the converse of 'If a figure is a square, then it is a rectangle'?
choices: If a figure is not a square, then it is not a rectangle
If a figure is a square, then it is not a rectangle
If a figure is a rectangle, then it is a square

questions.question: Which figure disproves 'Every rectangle is a square'?
Which statement is an example of deductive reasoning?
choices: Several measured triangles suggest an angle-sum pattern
A triangle's angles total 180°, so the third angle is 70° when the others are 50° and 60°
A shape looks symmetric, so it probably is
Three examples make every quadrilateral a rectangle

questions.question: Why should a diagram not be assumed to be drawn to scale?
choices: Visual appearance may not match the stated measurements
Angles cannot be shown in drawings
Only circles can be drawn accurately

questions.question: If AB = CD, what justifies replacing AB with CD in an equation?
Which condition is needed before using corresponding-angle equality to prove two lines parallel?
choices: The lines must already be labeled parallel
The angles must both be acute
The angles must be corresponding angles formed by the same transversal

questions.question: Which statement uses inductive reasoning?
choices: Applying an established theorem to a specified triangle
Observing several cases and proposing a general pattern
Using equality substitution in a proof
Deriving a conclusion from given premises

questions.question: A student proves two triangles congruent and then concludes their corresponding sides are equal. What supports that final step?
choices: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal
Every pair of angles is supplementary

questions.question: Which example disproves 'If a quadrilateral has four equal sides, then it has four right angles'?
If a proof needs x = 4 but its steps show only x² = 16, what remains to be justified?
Why is the converse of a true statement not automatically true?
choices: A true statement has no hypothesis
Reversing the hypothesis and conclusion creates a different claim
A conclusion cannot be used as a hypothesis

questions.question: A student assumes the desired conclusion to justify an earlier step. What is the main problem?
choices: The argument has too many diagrams
